historical_growth.growth_rate_source: net_revenue_3yr_cagr, cross-checked to FY26 guidance (low-single-digit constant-currency net revenue growth)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable as the growth anchor: shareholders' equity is shrinking (-11.1% 3yr) because buybacks and dividends (GBP 2.8bn in FY2025) exceed retained profit, while reported EPS grows on impairment base effects and a falling share count. Adjusted EPS CAGR is 5.9% (3yr) / 4.4% (5yr), of which ~3-4pp is share-count reduction.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on Tobacco & NGP net revenue (FY2018-FY2025: 7,697 -> 8,316); reported revenue including duty is -0.4% (3yr). FCF CAGRs are on the owner series (OCF - capex - SBC - lease cash): 3yr 2.7% vs reported 3.1%, 5yr -3.1% vs -2.7% (FY2020 was a working-capital peak). SBC is too small to open a gap. Adjusted operating profit CAGR FY2018-FY2025 is 0.8%; FY2021-FY2025 2.8%.

scenario_narratives.base: Imperial keeps doing what it has done since 2021: combustible price/mix of 6-8% more than offsets 3-5% volume decline in its five priority markets (US, Germany, UK, Spain, Australia), aggregate share is roughly held, and NGP (blu, Zone, Pulze) grows double digit from a small base towards break-even without becoming a profit pillar. Net revenue grows ~2% to FY30 and adjusted operating profit ~3%, the low end of the 2030 Strategy range once FX is taken off, helped by the GBP 320m efficiency programme. After FY30 pricing power fades toward inflation-minus as the smoker base shrinks, growth settles at 0.5% and the exit is capped at 12x owner FCF. Leverage stays at 2.0-2.5x and all free cash goes out through the dividend and the evergreen buyback.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2030 Strategy is delivered at the top of its range: US pricing and share gains continue in a consolidated, rational market, AAACE grows volumes, and NGP reaches scale and positive contribution (modern oral in the US and Nordics, vapour in Europe) so that category decline is partly replaced rather than merely priced over. Net revenue grows 3-3.5% and margins expand ~4pp as efficiencies drop through and NGP losses disappear. Regulation stays incremental (no US nicotine cap, no generational bans in the big five), and the market grants a 14x terminal multiple to a business that has shown its cash flows are durable.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pricing model breaks. Excise shocks and affordability push down-trading and illicit trade (already acute in Australia and the UK), volume declines accelerate to 6-8%, and price increases no longer cover them, so net revenue turns negative from FY27 and falls 3% a year. Regulation bites in the profit pools that matter: a US menthol ban or nicotine cap, the UK generational smoking ban and vape restrictions, and EU TPD3/tobacco-excise-directive increases; NGP remains sub-scale and loss-making against PMI and BAT. Operating deleverage takes ~5pp off the margin, the duty float unwinds, and with net debt of GBP 10.5bn fixed against a shrinking EBITDA, leverage rises above 3x and the buyback stops. The exit is a 10x multiple on a perpetually declining stream.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Imperial is valued as a leveraged, slowly melting cash annuity, not a compounder: an unlevered owner-FCF stream of ~GBP 2.9bn built from adjusted EBITDA on net revenue (ex-duty), discounted at a GBP-built 7.5% WACC with the terminal multiple capped at 10-14x. Everything that is not a recurring flow is charged once in the equity bridge: the Logista minority at market value, the pension deficit, the remaining 2030 Strategy cash costs and the Delaware settlement. Because equity is the residual after GBP 10.5bn of net debt, per-share value is roughly 1.4x geared to enterprise value, which is why the bear case falls much further than the bull case rises relative to the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet vintage: anchors are from 31 Mar 2026, a seasonal high for net debt; FY2026 year-end results (30 Sep 2026) are not yet in the folder and will move net debt, the share count and the FY27 guide.
Terminal multiple: the cap binds in all three scenarios, so value is close to linear in the 10x/12x/14x choice; each 1x in the base case is worth roughly 200p per share.
Regulatory step-changes (US menthol/nicotine rules, UK generational ban, EU excise directive) are discontinuous and are only crudely represented by a smooth bear path.

Logista is deducted at a market value that has risen sharply; a lower Logista price raises Imperial's value on this method while lowering the value of its own 50.01% stake, which is embedded in the flows at a fixed margin.
Currency: net debt is materially all euro and most profit is USD/EUR, while the model is in GBP with no explicit FX path.
FY2025 cash tax (16.4%) was well below the 24% modelled; if low cash tax persists, the flows are understated by ~GBP 300m a year.

inputs.share_count_basis: Period-end 31 Mar 2026: 844,313,254 issued (HY26 note, after cancellations) less 62,589,137 treasury shares (FY2025 Directors' report; buybacks are cancelled, so the treasury block is static) = 781.7m, plus 5.7m potentially dilutive share options (HY26 EPS note) = 787.4m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; the evergreen buyback (GBP 1.45bn in FY26) is debt/FCF-funded capital return, treated as value-neutral.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based payments add-back GBP 35m (note 27 shows 36m). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). Model -> quote conversion is the fixed 100 pence per pound, not a market FX rate. Unsuffixed per-share values are in pence and comparable to current_price. Logista NCI converted at EURGBP 0.8347 (Yahoo EURGBP=X, 2026-11-19).
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP build: 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, ~5.5% ERP, tobacco equity beta ~0.8 -> cost of equity ~8.9%; pre-tax debt ~4.5% (materially all euro-denominated after swaps), ~3.4% after tax; debt ~32% of capital at market values -> ~7.1%, rounded up to 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: regulatory and volume risk is carried in the scenario flows and the capped terminal multiple, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal 94 + interest 15 = 109, 1.3% of net revenue) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (404 at 31 Mar 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (311 adjusted D&A less 101 ROU = 210, 2.5%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Logista (50.01% owned, fully consolidated) is in the flows at 100%; the 49.99% minority is deducted once in the equity bridge at market value. No leakage is applied to the flows. NCI dividends (156 in FY2025) are therefore not deducted from the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US; adaptations applied for GBP/GBp quote, leases, NCI, pension). REVENUE BASE: Tobacco & NGP net revenue (GBP 8,316m FY2025, KPI NetRevenue), NOT reported revenue of GBP 32.2bn which is 59% excise duty plus Logista pass-through. All percent paths are group cash items divided by T&NGP net revenue, so the EBITDA margin (adjusted EBITDA 4,299 / 8,316 = 51.7%) includes Logista's contribution and is not a peer-comparable segment margin. EBITDA is the company's ADJUSTED EBITDA (adjusted operating profit + depreciation/software amortisation; acquired-intangible amortisation of ~358 is non-cash and excluded); adjusting cash items are handled in the bridge instead. NET DEBT: reported net debt 10,943 at 31 Mar 2026 less lease liabilities 404 = 10,539 (includes accrued interest and derivative fair values; company adjusted net debt is 10,518). SEASONALITY: March net debt is seasonally high (H1 working-capital outflow 1,336; 30 Sep 2025 adjusted net debt was 8,406; management expects ~2.0x at year end). Year 1 of the model is the full FY2026, half of which is already inside the March balance sheet, so the normalised H1 FY26 unlevered outflow is added back in the bridge. TIMING: FY2026 ended 30 Sep 2026 and its results are due/just released but are NOT in the research folder; year-1 flows are nonetheless discounted a full year from the valuation date, which understates value by roughly half a year of return (~3%). Refresh anchors (net debt, shares, FY27 guidance) when the FY2026 annual report is parsed. OWNER FCF: reported_fcf = OCF 3,627 - gross capex 384 (OCF is before interest paid, which IMB reports in financing, so it is unlevered); last_fcf = 3,243 - SBC 35; interest income not stripped (net-debt company). FY2025 cash tax paid (513, 16.4%) was abnormally low versus a 23-24% adjusted rate; the forward path uses the normal rate, so year-1 owner FCF (~2.9bn before specials) sits below the FY2025 actual. Company FCF guidance for FY26 (>= 2.2bn after ~480 interest, ~160 NCI dividends, ~300 of 2030-Strategy and Delaware cash) reconciles to ~3.0bn on this basis. Buybacks are funded (GBP 1,235m FY2025; GBP 809m H1 FY26), so the flat count is real. SBC is ~0.4% of net revenue: house and street bases are close to coincident. No Analysis JSON existed for this ticker; scenario axes are drawn from the FY2025 annual report, HY26 results and the May 2026 presentation.

bear.wc_note: The business runs on a duty-payable float (negative working capital); shrinking sales unwind it, so a decline in net revenue consumes cash.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/-2.0% gives 10.3x; the 10x cap binds marginally.

base.growth_rationale: FY26: low-single-digit constant-currency guidance less 0-1% FX headwind; H1 FY26 net revenue +1.8% reported. FY27-FY30 at the low end of the 2030 Strategy's low-single-digit ambition, then fading as combustible pricing has to work harder against 3-5% annual volume decline.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 adjusted operating profit +2.5% (below the 3-5% constant-currency guide after FX; H1 was -0.5% reported with an H2-weighted year) plus ~312 D&A = ~4,400. Then ~0.3-0.4pp a year to FY30 as the GBP 320m efficiency programme lands, flat afterwards.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted effective rate guided 23-24% for FY26 with stated upward pressure medium term; applied to unlevered EBIT.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/0.5% gives 14.4x, above the 12x cap, so the cap binds: a structurally declining-volume category is not granted a compounder's exit multiple.

bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/1.0% gives 15.5x; the 14x cap binds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: the equity sits behind GBP 10.5bn of net debt and depends on a single mechanism (price outrunning volume) that regulators and excise authorities in five markets can each impair. Base at 50%: it is essentially the continuation of the FY21-FY25 record and FY26 guidance. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs NGP to reach profitable scale, regulation to stay benign and a re-rating of the terminal multiple, three largely independent things.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
